**Type-level validation (SQL argument descriptors)** in `/workspace/repo/src/Functions/tokens.cpp`, `FunctionTokensOverloadResolver::getReturnTypeImpl`, lines 198-235. For a 3-arg call with `splitByString`, it registers the `separators` optional arg requiring `const Array` (lines 216-217):


**Value extraction** in `/workspace/repo/src/Functions/tokens.cpp`, `createTokenizer`, lines 29-71. Non-UInt args are pulled as a `ColumnArray` and pushed as a `Field` into `params` (lines 51-67), which is passed to `TokenizerFactory::instance().get(tokenizer_str, params)`.

**The actual parse + validate of the separator array** is in `TokenizerFactory.cpp` lines 184-202:
```cpp
auto split_by_string_creator = [](const FieldVector & args) -> std::unique_ptr<ITokenizer>
{
    assertParamsCount(args.size(), 1, SplitByStringTokenizer::getExternalName());
    if (args.empty())
        return std::make_unique<SplitByStringTokenizer>(std::vector<String>{" "});

    auto array = castAs<Array>(args[0], "separators");
    std::vector<String> values;
    for (const auto & value : array)
        values.emplace_back(castAs<String>(value, "separator"));

    if (values.empty())
        throw Exception(
            ErrorCodes::BAD_ARGUMENTS,
            "Incorrect parameter of tokenizer '{}': separators cannot be empty",
            SplitByStringTokenizer::getExternalName());

    return std::make_unique<SplitByStringTokenizer>(values);
};
```

## 3. Existing validation patterns for BAD_ARGUMENTS

All in `/workspace/repo/src/Interpreters/TokenizerFactory.cpp` (`ErrorCodes::BAD_ARGUMENTS` declared at line 17):

- **Type-checking helper** `castAs<Type>` at lines 24-36 — throws `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when the `Field` type doesn't match expected (used for `Array`, `String`, `UInt64`).
- **Argument-count helper** `assertParamsCount` at lines 38-47 — throws `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when too many params.
- **Non-empty-array check** for `splitByString` separators at lines 195-199 (shown above).
- **Range/relationship checks** as further examples of the pattern: `ngrams` min-size check at lines 161-167; `sparseGrams` min/max/cutoff checks at lines 232-260.

The idiomatic pattern for reporting a bad separators argument (e.g. empty array, wrong element type) is exactly the `split_by_string_creator` lambda: use `castAs<Array>`/`castAs<String>` for type validation and `throw Exception(ErrorCodes::BAD_ARGUMENTS, "Incorrect parameter of tokenizer '{}': ...", SplitByStringTokenizer::getExternalName())` for semantic validation."}
